metadata.summary: Multi-stage attack graph centered on CVE-2017-12477 (bpserverd authentication bypass). The graph reveals three primary attack vectors: (1) Initial Access through authentication bypasses and command injections, (2) Privilege Escalation through multiple local and remote techniques, (3) Persistence and Lateral Movement through database exploitation and file system manipulation. Critical attack chains include: unauthenticated RCE → privilege escalation → database compromise → persistent backdoor installation.

nodes.description: It was discovered that the bpserverd proprietary protocol in Unitrends Backup (UB) before 10.0.0, as invoked through xinetd, has an issue in which its authentication can be bypassed. A remote attacker could use this issue to execute arbitrary commands with root privilege on the target system.
nodes.vulnerability_type: Authentication Bypass leading to Remote Code Execution
nodes.precondition: network access to bpserverd service through xinetd
nodes.postcondition: arbitrary command execution with root privileges

nodes.description: It was discovered that the api/storage web interface in Unitrends Backup (UB) before 10.0.0 has an issue in which one of its input parameters was not validated. A remote attacker could use this flaw to bypass authentication and execute arbitrary commands with root privilege on the target system.
nodes.vulnerability_type: Input Validation Bypass leading to Authentication Bypass and RCE
nodes.precondition: network access to api/storage web interface
nodes.postcondition: authentication bypassed and arbitrary commands executed with root privileges

nodes.description: It was discovered that an issue in the session logic in Unitrends Backup (UB) before 10.0.0 allowed using the LOGDIR environment variable during a web session to elevate an existing low-privilege user to root privileges. A remote attacker with existing low-privilege credentials could then execute arbitrary commands with root privileges.
nodes.vulnerability_type: Privilege Escalation via Environment Variable Manipulation
nodes.precondition: low-privilege user credentials and active web session
nodes.postcondition: root privileges obtained and arbitrary command execution

nodes.description: It was discovered that the Unitrends Backup (UB) before 10.1.0 user interface was exposed to an authentication bypass, which then could allow an unauthenticated user to inject arbitrary commands into its /api/hosts parameters using backquotes.
nodes.vulnerability_type: Authentication Bypass leading to Command Injection
nodes.precondition: network access to user interface /api/hosts endpoint
nodes.postcondition: authentication bypassed and arbitrary command injection via backquotes

nodes.description: An issue was discovered in the server software in Kaseya Unitrends Backup Software before 10.5.5-2. There is a privilege escalation from read-only user to admin.
Kaseya Unitrends Client/Agent through 10.5,5 allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code.
An issue was discovered in the server software in Kaseya Unitrends Backup Software before 10.5.5-2. There is authenticated remote code execution.

An issue was discovered in Kaseya Unitrends Backup Appliance before 10.5.5. Multiple functions in the bpserverd daemon were vulnerable to arbitrary remote code execution as root. The vulnerability was caused by untrusted input (received by the server) being passed to system calls.
nodes.vulnerability_type: Remote Code Execution via Command Injection
nodes.precondition: ability to send untrusted input to bpserverd daemon

nodes.description: An issue was discovered in Kaseya Unitrends Backup Appliance before 10.5.5. A world writable file allowed local users to execute arbitrary code as the user apache, leading to privilege escalation.
nodes.vulnerability_type: Local Privilege Escalation via Insecure File Permissions

nodes.description: An issue was discovered in Kaseya Unitrends Backup Appliance before 10.5.5. Two unauthenticated SQL injection vulnerabilities were discovered, allowing arbitrary SQL queries to be injected and executed under the postgres superuser account. Remote code execution was possible, leading to full access to the postgres user account.
nodes.vulnerability_type: Unauthenticated SQL Injection leading to RCE
nodes.precondition: network access to vulnerable SQL endpoints
nodes.postcondition: postgres superuser access obtained and remote code execution

nodes.description: An issue was discovered in Kaseya Unitrends Backup Appliance before 10.5.5. The password for the PostgreSQL wguest account is weak.
nodes.precondition: knowledge of weak password or brute force capability

nodes.description: An issue was discovered in Kaseya Unitrends Backup Appliance before 10.5.5. The Unitrends Windows agent was vulnerable to DLL injection and binary planting due to insecure default permissions. This allowed privilege escalation from an unprivileged user to SYSTEM.
nodes.vulnerability_type: DLL Injection / Binary Planting leading to Privilege Escalation
nodes.precondition: unprivileged user access on Windows system with Unitrends agent

nodes.description: An issue was discovered in Kaseya Unitrends Backup Appliance before 10.5.5. The wguest account could execute commands by injecting into PostgreSQL trigger functions. This allowed privilege escalation from the wguest user to the postgres user.
nodes.vulnerability_type: Privilege Escalation via SQL Trigger Injection
nodes.postcondition: postgres user privileges obtained via trigger function injection

nodes.description: An issue was discovered in Kaseya Unitrends Backup Appliance before 10.5.5. The Samba file sharing service allowed anonymous read/write access.
nodes.postcondition: anonymous read/write access to file shares

nodes.description: An issue was discovered in Kaseya Unitrends Backup Appliance before 10.5.5. The privileged vaultServer could be leveraged to create arbitrary writable files, leading to privilege escalation.
nodes.vulnerability_type: Arbitrary File Write leading to Privilege Escalation
nodes.precondition: ability to interact with privileged vaultServer
nodes.postcondition: arbitrary file creation and privilege escalation

nodes.description: An issue was discovered in Kaseya Unitrends Backup Appliance before 10.5.5. A crafted HTTP request could induce a format string vulnerability in the privileged vaultServer application.
nodes.precondition: ability to send crafted HTTP requests to vaultServer
nodes.postcondition: potential code execution in privileged vaultServer context

nodes.description: An issue was discovered in Kaseya Unitrends Backup Appliance before 10.5.5. A buffer overflow existed in the vaultServer component. This was exploitable by a remote unauthenticated attacker.
An issue was discovered in Kaseya Unitrends Backup Appliance before 10.5.5. The apache user could read arbitrary files such as /etc/shadow by abusing an insecure Sudo rule.
nodes.vulnerability_type: Arbitrary File Read via Sudo Misconfiguration
nodes.postcondition: ability to read sensitive files including /etc/shadow

nodes.description: An issue was discovered in Kaseya Unitrends Backup Appliance before 10.5.5. The SNMP daemon was configured with a weak default community.
nodes.postcondition: unauthorized SNMP access and information disclosure

links.description: After gaining root RCE via bpserverd auth bypass, attacker can establish web session with low-privilege user (created via initial RCE) and use LOGDIR environment variable manipulation for additional privilege persistence and credential harvesting

Both vulnerabilities target bpserverd daemon with authentication bypass leading to root RCE. CVE-2021-43033 represents evolved attack vector through command injection in multiple functions, showing persistent architectural weakness in same component across versions

Both provide unauthenticated remote root access through different attack surfaces (api/storage vs bpserverd). Attacker can use either as initial compromise vector depending on network exposure and defensive controls

Similar exploitation pattern targeting web API endpoints with authentication bypass leading to command injection. Evolution from api/storage input validation flaw to /api/hosts backquote injection shows persistent API security weaknesses

After escalating to root via LOGDIR manipulation and establishing apache user access, attacker can abuse Sudo misconfiguration to read /etc/shadow for credential harvesting and lateral movement preparation

Session-based privilege escalation enables attacker to identify and exploit world-writable files for establishing persistent apache user backdoor, maintaining access after initial compromise detection

Command injection via authentication bypass allows creation of read-only users or discovery of existing credentials, which can then be escalated to admin through CVE-2021-40385 privilege escalation vulnerability

Both represent command injection vulnerabilities with different vectors (backquote injection vs system call injection). Demonstrates persistent pattern of unsafe input handling in Unitrends codebase across different components and versions

After escalating from read-only to admin via CVE-2021-40385, attacker gains sufficient privileges to exploit authenticated RCE in CVE-2021-40387, transforming limited access into complete system compromise

Admin-level privileges obtained through privilege escalation provide access to database configuration and credentials, enabling exploitation of SQL injection vulnerabilities for deeper system penetration
RCE on client/agent enables attacker to deploy DLL injection payloads on Windows systems, escalating from remote code execution to SYSTEM privileges for complete endpoint control
Compromise of backup agent provides credentials and network paths to backup server, enabling authenticated RCE on server infrastructure through trust relationships
Authenticated RCE on server combined with bpserverd command injection provides multiple simultaneous execution contexts, maximizing attacker's operational security and persistence options
Authenticated RCE provides initial access to exploit world-writable files for apache user privilege escalation, establishing persistent local foothold independent of initial access credentials
Root RCE through bpserverd enables creation of apache user context or direct exploitation of Sudo misconfiguration for /etc/shadow access, facilitating credential harvesting for lateral movement
Root-level command injection in bpserverd can be used to manipulate vaultServer interactions, exploiting arbitrary file write capability for additional persistence mechanisms and system modification

After gaining apache user access via world-writable file exploitation, attacker leverages Sudo misconfiguration for sensitive file reading including password hashes, enabling offline cracking and privilege escalation

SQL injection with postgres superuser access enables discovery and exploitation of weak wguest account credentials, providing additional database access vectors and credential harvesting opportunities
Unauthenticated SQL injection provides postgres superuser access which can create or discover wguest account, then exploit trigger function injection for persistent database-level backdoors
Weak wguest credentials provide legitimate database access that enables SQL trigger injection for privilege escalation to postgres user, transforming weak authentication into full database control

Postgres user privileges obtained through trigger injection can be leveraged to exploit apache user's Sudo misconfiguration through database-driven system command execution, bridging database and OS privilege contexts

Anonymous Samba write access enables planting malicious code in world-writable files, which when executed by local users triggers privilege escalation to apache user, combining network and local attack vectors
Anonymous Samba access on Windows agents facilitates DLL injection payload delivery without authentication, enabling remote attacker to plant malicious DLLs for SYSTEM privilege escalation

VaultServer arbitrary file write capability can be used to create or modify world-writable files that are exploited by CVE-2021-43034, providing controlled file content for reliable privilege escalation payload delivery

Format string vulnerability in vaultServer enables initial code execution or information disclosure that facilitates exploitation of arbitrary file write capability, chaining memory corruption with file system attacks

Both represent memory corruption vulnerabilities in vaultServer component (format string vs buffer overflow), providing redundant attack vectors against the same privileged service for reliability and evasion

Unauthenticated buffer overflow can be chained with format string vulnerability for more reliable exploitation, combining information leakage (format string) with control flow hijacking (buffer overflow)

Unauthenticated buffer overflow in vaultServer provides initial code execution context to exploit arbitrary file write capability for persistent backdoor installation and system configuration modification

Reading /etc/shadow via Sudo misconfiguration provides password hashes that enable local user credential compromise, which can then exploit world-writable files for privilege escalation to apache user

Weak SNMP community strings enable network reconnaissance and system information gathering including database configuration details, facilitating targeted SQL injection attacks against discovered database endpoints

SNMP access reveals file share configurations and network topology information that guides exploitation of anonymous Samba access, enabling attacker to identify high-value targets for file system manipulation

SYSTEM privileges on Windows agents via DLL injection enables creation of world-writable files on Linux backup server during backup operations, facilitating cross-platform attack propagation and persistence
